core_obligations: Choose an ideal of definition I of A and a fundamental system of open ideals I_lambda (proof lines 1442-1444).
Use tautness to see that the closure J of IB is open and that the closures J_lambda of I_lambda B are open and form a fundamental system of open ideals of B (proof lines 1445-1447).
For every lambda produce n with I^n contained in I_lambda, from the defining property of an ideal of definition (proof line 1448).
Observe that J^n lies in the closure of I^n B, hence J^n is contained in J_lambda, and conclude that J is an ideal of definition of B (proof lines 1449-1451).
proof_roadmap: Pick an ideal of definition and a fundamental system of open ideals in the source (proof lines 1442-1444).
Tautness gives openness and a fundamental system in the target (proof lines 1445-1447).
Sandwich the powers of the closure of IB between the J_lambda and conclude (proof lines 1448-1451).
difficulty_reason: For a continuous homomorphism of linearly topologized rings, tautness together with pre-admissibility of the source implies pre-admissibility of the target (statement lines 1435-1440). The proof produces the ideal of definition of the target outright: an ideal of definition I of A and a fundamental system of open ideals I_lambda are chosen, tautness gives that the closure J of IB is open and that the closures J_lambda of I_lambda B are open and form a fundamental system of open ideals of B (proof lines 1442-1447), the comparison I^n contained in I_lambda is used to sandwich the powers of J into the J_lambda, and J is concluded to be an ideal of definition (proof lines 1448-1451). The level is H2 because the argument is a short but genuine chase with the two defining properties of tautness and of an ideal of definition.
